messages:
maria: quick sync — after the chunk-size change on canary we're seeing weird user-facing pauses. raw token latency per-op looks fine but users report stutters :thinking:
ajay: saw the alert from perf-bot. p95 up slightly, p99 spikes much larger. link: https://internal.perf/reports/1859123456
taylor: can you paste the exact config you rolled? microbatch size, flush interval, kernel hints?
maria: rolled: microbatch=8, flush_ms=60, chunk_tokens=16, kv_prefetch=on. kernel_policy=auto (we let runtime pick)
ken: interesting — auto kernel picks a different SIMD path for short sequences. that can increase jitter if it falls back mid-epoch.
sofia: do we have traces showing time-to-first-byte vs inter-chunk gap? perceived latency usually from gaps between emitted chunks, not token compute
maria: attaching short trace excerpt:
```
emit_0: 24ms
emit_1: 48ms
emit_2: 320ms <-- big gap
emit_3: 26ms
```
ajay: gap at emit_2 aligns with kernel_selection() call in profiler. fallback to reference kernel when batch shape changes.
taylor: oh — microbatching variance + kv-cache misses can change sequence_len distribution per microbatch and trigger different kernel choices
ken: yes. when kv cache is cold, we're also incurring extra memcpy and cache refill which amplifies gap
sofia: propose experiments: 1) lock kernel to the low-latency kernel for canary 2) reduce flush_ms to 30ms 3) increase chunk_tokens to 32 to reduce frequent emits
maria: can we do 1) and 2) together on a ~1% traffic canary? worried about throughput cost
ajay: do it. we need to prioritize p99 for this flow. cost hit for 1% traffic is fine for now
perf-bot: regression alert — p99 token latency +540ms in production canary (relative +320%), top stack: kernel_selector -> kv_refill -> emit_scheduler
taylor: also add a metric: inter_emit_stddev per-request. helps quantify perceived stutter
ken: small note: when we push chunk_tokens to 32, perceived TTF (time-to-first-token) increases slightly for short responses. tradeoff
sofia: maybe hybrid emit: always send first N tokens asap (prefetch window) then batch rest every flush_ms. That keeps TTF low and reduces inter-chunk jitter
maria: config prototype:
```
streaming:
  emit_first: 2
  flush_ms: 40
  chunk_tokens: 24
  kernel_hint: low_latency
```
ajay: also check KV cache policy: switch to proactive warm on hot prefixes for 10s after first hit. avoids cold refills mid-stream
taylor: note on metrics — break out p95/p99 by request length buckets (<=32, 33-128, >128). regressions often concentrated in mid-length range
ken: we should instrument kernel selection reasons in spans. add field kernel_reason: [shape_mismatch, quant_mode, mem_pressure]
maria: running canary now with emit_first=2 + flush_ms=40 + kernel_hint=low_latency. will report in 30m
sofia: set alert thresholds: p95>120ms or p99>400ms for the canary route
perf-bot: canary deployment started: deploy/1859123460 -> canary(1%)
ajay: small provocation — maybe the root cause is scheduling on the GPU with contention at microbatch boundaries. if microbatches cross CUDA streams we might get stalls
taylor: true. check kernel concurrency config: concurrent_kernels=2 may oversubscribe for larger microbatches
ken: if we force single kernel concurrency for this workload we might reduce jitter at cost of throughput; good for latency SLO
maria: initial canary numbers after 8 minutes: p95 down ~15ms, p99 down ~260ms. users still report occasional pauses but much less frequent
sofia: promising. please collect traces for remaining p99 cases to see if kv_refill still appears
ajay: logged one trace: kernel_selection stable, remaining gap appears at emit_scheduler waiting on next flush tick — we might need a jittered flush schedule to avoid aligned stalls
taylor: jittered flush_ms +/- 10ms could smooth spikes across requests
maria: deployed jittered flush (+/-10ms) on a follow-up canary
perf-bot: canary update: p99 further improved (-120ms). total CPU cost +4%, GPU utilization slightly down (better packing)
ken: conclusion draft: perceived latency here driven by two orthogonal issues: kernel switching penalties (due to shape + kv cold) and synchronized flush boundaries causing aligned stalls. mitigations: lock low-latency kernel, hybrid-first-token emit, jittered flush, proactive kv warm
sofia: add a long-term fix: make kernel_selector cost-aware (penalize switching mid-stream) and expose per-customer kernel pinning in Dedicated
maria: I'll write up runbook and canary checklist. want to include exact config diffs and tracing links
taylor: assign to eng-runtime backlog: KERNEL-212 (selector heuristics), STREAM-88 (hybrid emit + jitter), KV-145 (proactive warm)
ajay: thanks all. nice cross-team debugging :thumbsup: 
maria: leaving this thread open until we close canary. will post final numbers
perf-bot: canary metrics snapshot: p95=98ms, p99=312ms, tail_error_rate=0.02% (improved)
